  • Class
    Description
    Attributes
    Typed values carried with a request, such as the request id or the authenticated user, set by middleware and read by handlers.
    Attributes.Key<T>
    A key for values of type T; declare it once, as a constant.
    Body
    A message body: bytes in memory, a blocking InputStream (how a backend hands over a request body), or a Body.Writer that writes straight to the connection (a streamed response).
    Body.Bytes
     
    Body.Guarded
    What a writer writes to: everything passes through, but close() does nothing (the backend closes the connection's stream), and so does flush() unless the body streams.
    Body.Input
     
    Body.Output
    A written body; flushes is whether the writer's flushes reach the connection.
    Body.Writer
    Writes a streamed response body.
    DecodeFailure
    A body that couldn't be decoded: 400 by default, 415 for a media type or charset the decoder doesn't support.
    Dsl
    The routing DSL: import static forj.http.Dsl.*; then
    Dsl.Handler0<F>
    An effectful handler for a path with 0 typed values.
    Dsl.Handler1<F,A>
    An effectful handler for a path with 1 typed value.
    Dsl.Handler2<F,A,B>
    An effectful handler for a path with 2 typed values.
    Dsl.Handler3<F,A,B,C>
    An effectful handler for a path with 3 typed values.
    Dsl.Handler4<F,A,B,C,D>
    An effectful handler for a path with 4 typed values.
    Dsl.On0
    A method and a path with 0 typed values, waiting for its handler.
    Dsl.On1<A>
    A method and a path with 1 typed value, waiting for its handler.
    Dsl.On2<A,B>
    A method and a path with 2 typed values, waiting for its handler.
    Dsl.On3<A,B,C>
    A method and a path with 3 typed values, waiting for its handler.
    Dsl.On4<A,B,C,D>
    A method and a path with 4 typed values, waiting for its handler.
    Dsl.Pure0
    A pure handler for a path with 0 typed values.
    Dsl.Pure1<A>
    A pure handler for a path with 1 typed value.
    Dsl.Pure2<A,B>
    A pure handler for a path with 2 typed values.
    Dsl.Pure3<A,B,C>
    A pure handler for a path with 3 typed values.
    Dsl.Pure4<A,B,C,D>
    A pure handler for a path with 4 typed values.
    Entity
    An encoded body and its media type: what an EntityEncoder produces, and what Ok(...) and friends put on a response.
    EntityDecoder<A>
    How to read an A from a body: a type class, so User u = req.as(); finds the decoder for User at compile time.
    EntityEncoder<A>
    How to write an A as a body: a type class, so Ok(value) finds the encoder for the value's type at compile time.
    Headers
    Immutable HTTP headers: names are case-insensitive, a name can repeat, and order is kept.
    HttpApp<F>
    What a server runs: a request in, an F of the response out.
    HttpFailure
    An expected failure with an HTTP answer: throw it (or raise it in F) from a handler, and the errors middleware responds with its status and message as a problem response.
    MediaType
    A media type, as in a Content-Type header: text/plain; charset=utf-8.
    Method
    An HTTP request method.
    Middleware<F>
    Wraps an app: cross-cutting behaviour (errors, request ids, logging, timeouts, CORS, auth) as plain function composition.
    Path
    Where typed route paths start: Path.root().then("users").then(LongVar), or Path.of("/users").then(LongVar), is a Path1<Long>.
    Path0
    A route path with no typed segments.
    Path1<A>
    A route path capturing 1 typed value: A, in order.
    Path2<A,B>
    A route path capturing 2 typed values: A, B, in order.
    Path3<A,B,C>
    A route path capturing 3 typed values: A, B, C, in order.
    Path4<A,B,C,D>
    A route path capturing 4 typed values: A, B, C, D, in order.
    Problem
    An RFC 9457 problem response (application/problem+json): how forj-http reports errors.
    Query
    Decoded query parameters, in order: a=1&b=x+y&a=2.
    Request
    An HTTP request: immutable, with with* copy methods.
    RequestContext
    What every part of a request's handling may need to know about the request: its id, for logs and for the calls it makes downstream.
    Response
    An HTTP response: a plain, immutable value, never an F.
    Route<F>
    One method and path with its handler, made with Dsl: GET(path).to(...) or GET(path).respond(...).
    Routes<F>
    Routes compiled into a path trie: matching costs one step per path segment, however many routes there are, instead of trying each route in turn.
    Segment
    One segment of a route's path: a fixed Segment.Literal or a typed Var.
    Segment.Literal
    Matches exactly this (decoded) text.
    Status
    An HTTP status code and its reason phrase.
    Uri
    A request target in origin form: a path and an optional query, as sent on the request line (/users/7?verbose=1).
    Var<A>
    A typed path segment: Path.of("/users").then(LongVar) matches /users/7 and hands the handler a long.
